title: Observability & security maturity assessment
summary: A maturity assessment across observability and security spanning 11 domains — quantifying current-state coverage and producing a defensible improvement path for engineering leadership.

sections.challenge: MELI's observability and security posture spanned 11 domains, more than 12 billion documents, 1,459 detection rules, and 102 agents reporting 100% coverage — a large, mature-looking footprint by volume. A structured maturity assessment was needed to separate genuine operational maturity from sheer scale. The assessment found impact analysis for rule and pipeline changes was still 100% manual — a process gap, not a capability, and one that does not scale safely with the data volume already in place.
sections.architecture: The assessment measured maturity against a 4-stage model (current score: 1.8 / 4.0), covering detection coverage, pipeline observability (OpenTelemetry instrumentation flowing from source through collector to backend), and operational process maturity across the 11 domains.
sections.implementation: Maturity scoring combined rule-coverage audits (1,459 MITRE-mapped detection rules), agent fleet verification (102 agents, 100% coverage), and an OpenTelemetry pipeline review (source → collector → backend) to establish a baseline before any remediation work.
sections.results: 12B+ documents and 1,459 detection rules were confirmed under 100% agent coverage (102 agents) across 11 domains. The maturity model placed the organization at 1.8 / 4.0, with the clearest gap being the fully manual impact-analysis process for rule and pipeline changes.
lessons: Coverage metrics (102 agents, 100% reporting) measure presence, not maturity — they should never be read as a maturity score on their own.
A 1.8/4.0 maturity score with 12B+ docs under management shows scale and maturity are independent axes worth measuring separately.
100% manual impact analysis is the highest-leverage finding: it is a process gap that compounds risk as rule count grows, not a strength to highlight.
Mapping rules to MITRE ATT&CK before scoring made coverage gaps visible in a way raw rule counts could not.
